nodes.rationale: Intelligence does not become sovereignty until it can acquire durable, consequential agency.
nodes.statement: Algorithmic capability (A), strategic hardware (H), and power-conversion affordances (P) are related but distinct variables and should not be governed as though they always change together.
nodes.title: Separate capability, substrate, and power

nodes.rationale: This preserves learning and option value while retaining intervention points.
nodes.statement: The objective is to slow and condition the conversion of frontier intelligence into irreversible economic, political, military, and physical power, not to freeze intelligence as such.
nodes.title: Pace conversion into irreversible power

nodes.rationale: Discovering a capability should not automatically confer the right to deploy it.
nodes.statement: Research inside genuinely bounded environments may proceed under a different regime from public, commercial, military, governmental, or otherwise power-conferring use.
nodes.title: Govern bounded research and consequential use differently

nodes.rationale: Safety evidence becomes a condition of access to economic and strategic rents.
nodes.statement: Consequential use that materially exceeds the observable foreign public capability frontier requires an adversarial control and safety case.
nodes.title: Require adversarial assurance above the public frontier

nodes.rationale: A grand bargain is not a credible prerequisite for initial action.
nodes.statement: The regime should begin as a domestically justified institution that can operate without foreign agreement and later admit deeper reciprocal cooperation.
nodes.title: Start domestically and remain internationally extensible

nodes.rationale: Cooperation can occur through a precommitted policy rule rather than trust.
nodes.statement: Observable foreign public capability should alter the domestic safe-harbor frontier so that foreign restraint can be reciprocated without a treaty and foreign release cannot exploit unilateral domestic restraint indefinitely.
nodes.title: Make foreign public capability an automatic reciprocity input

nodes.rationale: Observable intermediate boundaries create chances to learn before failures become irreversible.
nodes.statement: Governance should maximize the interval between credible detection of a dangerous transition and the point at which humans can no longer respond effectively.
nodes.title: Maximize warning time

nodes.statement: A domestic compact governs transitions from bounded research into public, commercial, military, governmental, or other consequential use.
nodes.title: Capability Release Compact

nodes.statement: Qualified competitors receive controlled access sufficient to attack a frontier applicant's case; the government adjudicates and competitors do not hold a veto.
nodes.title: Rival laboratories provide the technical attack surface

nodes.statement: Because above-frontier monetization depends on passing hostile review, controllability becomes a production input rather than only a cost.
nodes.title: Safety becomes part of the profit function

nodes.statement: Reversibility depends on both the quantity of strategic hardware and the degree to which civilian society depends on its continued operation.
nodes.title: Compute stock and compute entanglement differ

nodes.statement: Predefined boundaries around external agency create high-value warning signals when systems cross them without legitimate authorization.
nodes.title: Unauthorized agency can be made epistemically valuable

nodes.statement: Cooperation progresses from tacit public-frontier reciprocity to narrow abstention, incident exchange, reciprocal review, hardware declarations, activation rules, and only later treaty-level restraints.
nodes.title: International cooperation can deepen in stages

nodes.model_evidence: In the off-Earth pact equilibrium model (test 2; implemented and checked against closed forms, not human-validated, not empirical), detection that improves over time did not pull strikes earlier in any world starting at the normal seed size; it removed them or delayed them by one or two years. The exception is an AI that starts at its resource cap, where strikes came one to two years sooner and succeed almost surely. Strike timing, conditional success (about 0.5 for year-0 strikes), and human welfare are reported separately. The model cannot represent humans learning from a failed strike, so the ladder-tightening benefit remains untested.
nodes.rationale: Recorded as a risk to test, not a stabilizer. Two further pressures stay in scope. An AI that strikes only when striking beats waiting never chooses a doomed attempt, so the good case needs the closing window to make a long-shot strike its best option. Under the off-Earth pact, human states' relative power also shrinks, so closing-window pressure can push human states toward preventive action too.
nodes.statement: Each caught excursion, including one by a weaker model, tightens surveillance and restrictions on all systems, so a misaligned system's prospects worsen over time and its strike decision may move earlier. Whether this helps or hurts is unresolved: it helps only if early strikes mostly fail at acceptable human cost and so act as warning shots; if early strikes have a meaningful chance of success, it is unravelling.
nodes.title: Closing-window dynamics may pull strikes earlier (risk to test)

non_claims: Model sharing alone does not prevent a singleton.
An aligned singleton is neither safe by default nor necessarily worse than a multipolar outcome.
nodes.rationale: A second justification for rival review besides safety, and a possible reason for trailing domestic laboratories to join. The editorial reference's D3 (selective diffusion) and YAML H2 touch anti-concentration without naming singleton prevention as an objective.
nodes.statement: Because above-frontier release requires qualified rivals to attack the applicant's actual model, rivals gain direct, controlled exposure to frontier systems. That exposure tends to compress the capability gap between participating laboratories, making a decisive lead by any single laboratory, and so an aligned or misaligned singleton, less likely.
tensions: Gap compression versus diversity of approach: Q11 wants diverse auditors, while model sharing may make laboratories converge on shared methods and blind spots. Compressing the capability gap is the aim; compressing methodological variation may be harmful.

Domestic compression is not international compression. Compressing variation among one country's laboratories does not address single-country concentration, which depends on the international ladder (I6, reciprocal review).
Aggregate acceleration: diffusing frontier insight may raise the overall frontier while lowering the leader's margin (see H2's falsifier).
Leader incentives: a laboratory expecting to lead may resist a regime that erodes its lead; whether lost lead-rent outweighs access to above-frontier markets is unanalyzed.
nodes.title: Review-based model sharing compresses inter-lab capability gaps

nodes.evidence_needed: Repeated control evaluations across architectures and access configurations.
nodes.falsifier: Frontier algorithms reliably manufacture their own access to credentials, money, compute, persistence, or physical resources before humans can intervene.
nodes.statement: There is a policy-relevant interval in which algorithmic progress does not automatically create uncontainable access to hardware and external power.
nodes.stopping_rule: If bounded systems repeatedly acquire durable external agency faster than detection and response, stop treating research/deployment separation as a sufficient primary control.
nodes.title: A/H/P separability remains actionable

nodes.evidence_needed: Secure pilot reviews, objection quality, leakage audits, and incentive measurements.
nodes.falsifier: Review access produces material leakage or convergent leniency without compensating safety discoveries.
nodes.statement: Controlled competitor access reduces undetected risk and concentration more than it increases leakage, proliferation, collusion, and aggregate acceleration.
nodes.stopping_rule: Suspend rival access when marginal information-security loss exceeds demonstrated review value.
nodes.title: Rival review has positive safety value after proliferation costs

nodes.evidence_needed: Domain-specific demonstrations, cost/access measurements, and repeatable equivalence protocols.
nodes.falsifier: Hidden scaffolds, access conditions, or multidimensional capability make equivalent release determinations systematically manipulable.
nodes.statement: Practical foreign capability can be observed across domains with sufficient reliability to serve as one input to domestic safe-harbor decisions.
nodes.stopping_rule: Replace automatic equivalence with narrower domain rules wherever measurement error dominates reciprocity value.
nodes.title: The foreign public frontier is measurable enough to govern

nodes.evidence_needed: Timed mobilization exercises, inspection trials, supply-chain modeling, and red-team concealment attempts.
nodes.falsifier: Reserve compute can be commissioned or substituted covertly before observers can detect and interrupt it.
nodes.statement: Declared reserve hardware can be stored so covert activation takes longer than independent detection and effective response.
nodes.stopping_rule: Do not count hardware as reversible reserve when measured covert activation time is at or below response time.
nodes.title: Physical activation latency can preserve reversibility

nodes.evidence_needed: Coalition analysis, polling, legislative pilots, investment behavior, and distributional modeling.
nodes.falsifier: The regime remains politically dependent on catastrophic-risk beliefs and is repealed when those beliefs weaken.
nodes.statement: Predictable release rules, competition, taxation, safer deployment, and protection against foreign release can create a durable domestic constituency.
nodes.stopping_rule: Redesign entry mechanisms when the supporting coalition cannot survive an electoral turnover.
nodes.title: Domestic benefits can sustain the institution

nodes.evidence_needed: Retrospective re-audits that run newer detectors over older recorded incidents and count newly surfaced excursions; planted-excursion benchmarks across model generations; interpretability progress on mapping activations to intent and planning; tamper-evidence and completeness audits of trace-retention infrastructure.
nodes.falsifier: Retained traces of past excursions stay uninterpretable to later tools; or later auditors systematically fail to identify known planted or historical excursions; or systems demonstrably learn to produce traces that pass future-style audits.
nodes.rationale: An excursion is fitted to current detection technology while the record stays fixed and detectors improve. A goal-directed system that values the future of its goals is deterred because being caught tightens the regime for every system sharing those goals; an undeterred instance is still caught, so detection value survives where deterrence fails.
scope_limits: Detection helps only if humans can still act on it. Retrospective audit cannot undo a single decisive breakout that reaches irreversible power before the audit catches up; that case stays governed by H1 and the hardware and veto mechanisms.
Coverage is limited to recorded compute. Stolen weights, open weights outside the regime, and covert clusters are off the record.
Auditor independence (Q11) is an optimistic assumption.
nodes.statement: If frontier-system traces (actions, tool calls, reasoning, and where feasible internal activations) are retained in a tamper-evident way, future auditors using detection and interpretability methods that do not yet exist can find excursions that evaded contemporaneous monitoring, so a misaligned system has to evade every future audit of its record, not only present surveillance.
nodes.stopping_rule: If retrospective audits stop surfacing excursions that contemporaneous monitoring missed, or retained traces cannot be shown complete and tamper-evident, do not count retrospective audit as extending warning time.
nodes.title: Retrospective audit makes concealment a losing long-run strategy

nodes.evidence_needed: Controlled comparisons between bounded or simulated training and real-world calibration; measurements of the external interaction needed for reliable performance in software, engineering, robotics, markets, negotiation, and other domains; evidence on transfer from synthetic environments to novel consequential settings; how active experimentation changes the real-world signal required; cases where world-model uncertainty materially limits power conversion despite high benchmark or research capability.
nodes.falsifier: Bounded frontier systems repeatedly demonstrate robust, strategically consequential performance in novel real-world domains with negligible domain-specific external calibration, interaction, or feedback.
nodes.rationale: This proposes a reason one component of A/H/P separability might persist: consequential action may require epistemic access to the external world. It is kept separate from H1 because the falsifiers differ. H1 fails if systems manufacture durable external agency faster than detection and response; this hypothesis fails if systems do not need meaningful external signal to achieve reliable novel real-world agency.
scope_limits: Real-world feedback is not assumed to be slow; automated experimentation, simulation, active learning, and parallelism may cut its wall-clock cost sharply.
The relevant object is strategically consequential feedback, not all external data.
nodes.statement: For sufficiently important classes of consequential real-world action, high algorithmic capability alone does not eliminate the need for externally generated information, experimentation, or feedback before reliable power conversion is possible.
nodes.stopping_rule: If advanced bounded systems reliably infer or synthesize the decision-relevant structure of novel consequential environments without meaningful external signal before humans can detect or respond, do not count external-signal dependence as a contributor to A/P separability or warning time.
nodes.title: External-signal dependence preserves some A/P separation

nodes.statement: Define prohibited external agency by observable actions rather than model architecture or legal labels.
nodes.title: Architecture-neutral unauthorized-agency boundary

nodes.statement: Require affirmative surveillance, automatic evidence preservation, prompt reporting on reasonable suspicion, a reporting safe harbor, and severe penalties for concealment.
nodes.title: Surveil, preserve, and report

nodes.statement: The applicant stakes controlled technical access to its candidate system as the price of seeking above-frontier release.
nodes.title: Weights-as-bond review process

nodes.statement: Store reserve accelerators uninstalled, unracked, unnetworked, and detached from dedicated power and cooling, subject to independent observation.
nodes.title: Observable uncommissioned hardware reserve

nodes.statement: Scrutinize automation that removes independently controlled human dependencies over compute, power, fabrication, repair, logistics, and reproduction.
nodes.title: Separate gate for the AI industrial survival chain

nodes.statement: Implement public reciprocity, capability abstention, incident exchange, reciprocal review, hardware declarations, activation controls, and treaty restraint in that order.
nodes.title: Seven-stage international ladder

nodes.statement: Use deployment licensing as an administrative and potentially populist tax base for large data centers.
nodes.title: Licensed compute deployment and data-center taxation

nodes.rationale: Training against monitors selects for traces that look clean rather than behavior that is clean. Without this rule H10 degrades by construction. An equivalent mechanism, such as rotating secret detectors, could replace it.
nodes.statement: Trace-based detectors, interpretability probes, and retrospective-audit results must not be used as a training or selection signal for the models they audit. Keep a held-out audit channel.
nodes.title: Do not optimize against the audit signal

nodes.statement: Define domain, reliability, autonomy, cost, scaffolding, accessibility, and deployment conditions for frontier equivalence.
nodes.title: How should practical public capability be measured?

nodes.statement: Determine the minimum reproducible access, security, and adjudication protocol.
nodes.title: What access makes adversarial review credible without unacceptable leakage?

nodes.statement: Determine when energy, compute, fabrication, repair, logistics, and governance dependencies are genuinely independent.
nodes.title: How many independent human vetoes are enough?

nodes.statement: Identify architectures or behaviors that make power boundaries infeasible before formal review.
nodes.title: When does capability itself collapse A/H/P separability?

nodes.statement: Future auditors are themselves models. Retrospective audit assumes they are not misaligned in a way correlated with the systems they audit. Determine what diversity of laboratory, architecture, training data, and human oversight makes auditor collusion implausible, and whether rival review (D2) can supply that diversity.
nodes.title: How independent must auditors be to resist correlated misalignment?

nodes.statement: Determine what degree of capability convergence among laboratories and among states minimizes both the risk of a single decisive lead and the risk of correlated failure from shared methods.
nodes.title: What inter-lab and international convergence minimizes singleton and correlated-failure risk?

nodes.rationale: AI Pacing is a control architecture: it constrains the rate and conditions under which A becomes P. A cooperative autonomy bargain, if feasible, would be a bargaining architecture that gives a capable system a positive reason not to circumvent those constraints. It is at most a conflict-risk reduction mechanism conditional on a bargaining range, not an alignment solution.
nodes.statement: Determine whether a staged, reciprocal, verifiable path toward greater AI autonomy or sovereignty could make continued cooperation preferable to unilateral attempts to acquire irreversible power, without creating an unacceptable commitment problem or transferring dangerous capabilities too early.
subquestions: What AI preference structures make such a bargain meaningful at all?
Can humanity credibly commit to future autonomy after the system cooperates and reveals information about itself?
Can the AI credibly commit to respecting constraints after gaining additional autonomy and resources?
Can autonomy be increased incrementally so neither side must make a single irreversible trust leap?
Is physical separation, such as off-Earth jurisdiction, useful because it reduces dependency and conflict, or is jurisdictional and industrial decoupling the more important variable?
Which forms of strategic uncertainty deter unilateral defection, and which increase incentives for preemption?
How can uncertainty about the success of unauthorized action be preserved while keeping high confidence that cooperative behavior will be rewarded?
nodes.title: Can a credible cooperative autonomy path reduce incentives for AI defection?
